title: Pandemic EBT raised sugary-item spending among lower-income households with children
published_window: 2026; public NBER LinkedIn feed excerpt within six months before retrieval
discussion_signal: The NBER feed excerpt translates the P-EBT paper into a consumer-allocation result: weekly sugary-item spending rose 16% among lower-income households with children, and the increase was about twice the increase in overall food spending. The signal is useful for the consumer/public-program chain because assistance changed the composition of purchases, not only the total food budget.
linked_research_question: When US food assistance replaces a constrained in-kind meal route with more flexible purchasing power, how do households, retailers, and product categories respond, and what happens to food security, health, and consumer choice?
limits: The retained URL is the NBER company feed because the indexed result exposed the exact post excerpt rather than a stable direct-post URL
Purchase data are not consumption, nutrition, health, or food-security outcomes
The feed excerpt does not report the panel count, effect interval, or full identification details
